description: Community-maintained superconducting parameters with literature citations, including Tc, Jc, critical fields, specific heat, gap and structure parameters. IEEE advertises thousands of materials; an independently verified record count, data export and dataset-wide license were not established. IEEE states that it verifies publication provenance rather than entry accuracy.

sources.evidence: Describes community property entries and explicitly limits its assurance to publication in peer-reviewed sources.

name: Roberts superconductive-materials survey (1976; literature through March 1975)
description: B. W. Roberts reference compilation of critical temperatures, critical fields, composition and crystal-structure types, including negative experiments. IEEE labels it by the 1975 literature cutoff; the publication is Journal of Physical and Chemical Reference Data 5, 581 (1976). Retained as a reference source rather than a separately counted modern dataset.

sources.title: Survey of superconductive materials and critical evaluation of selected properties
sources.evidence: Title/abstract identifies the 1976 publication, March 1975 literature cutoff and property tables.

name: Roberts Properties of Selected Superconductive Materials, 1978 Supplement
description: NBS Technical Note 983 supplements the earlier survey with literature through fall 1977, including Tc, critical fields, crystal structure and negative experiments. No independent structure or sample total is inferred from this publication.

sources.title: NIST Technical Note 983 publication record
sources.evidence: Official record confirms Roberts, 1978, title and DOI 10.6028/NBS.TN.983.

name: CERN STEAM Materials Library (SMaLi)
description: Collection of coded material-property functions for superconducting-magnet engineering, with C implementations and wrappers for Python, MATLAB, GetDP and COMSOL. Documentation includes HTS/LTS critical-current-density models. This is a model/software library, not a counted experimental crystal database.

sources.title: CERN STEAM Materials documentation
sources.evidence: Identifies material-property C code, wrappers, documentation and the CERN GitLab source repository.

sources.title: SMaLi reference documentation
sources.evidence: Documents superconducting critical current and HTS/LTS critical-current-density function families.

sources.title: IEEE CSC linked reference list
sources.evidence: Directory explicitly links the archived Wikipedia superconductors list PDF.

name: SCLib / JZIS superconducting-transition records
description: Additional primary-source lead outside the IEEE list. Public snapshot reports 13,282 transition results from 6,122 papers, with sample/criterion/condition provenance and CSV downloads. Model checks and sampled-batch checks are not individual expert validation. Project-created data use CC BY 4.0, while upstream-source terms remain applicable; no independent crystal count is claimed here.

sources.title: SCLib public materials snapshot
sources.evidence: 2026-10-31 version 98b37554e5a6 reports 13,282 results, 7,556 material entries counted separately per paper and 6,122 papers; model-review limitations are explicit.

sources.title: SCLib data license

sources.title: SCLib provenance and upstream-license notes

name: Materials Data Facility / Foundry
description: Materials-data publication and discovery services, with Foundry providing programmatic search and loading of machine-learning-ready deposits. Access and reuse conditions must be checked per deposit. Collection, file and record totals must not be summed as unique crystals. This is the canonical merged resource for the duplicate Materials Data Facility entries.

sources.title: Materials Data Facility
sources.evidence: Describes publication and discovery services and links Foundry. The non-www domain redirects here; both supplied routes returned the same final response body.

sources.title: Foundry — official source repository

sources.title: MDF publishing and discovery guides
sources.evidence: Retained from the existing catalog record as its original guide route; this supplement independently verified the homepage and Foundry source repository.

name: Computational Materials Repository (CMR)
description: DTU portal for project-specific ASE databases spanning low-dimensional materials, bulk crystals, perovskites, surfaces and related benchmarks. Provides project documentation, browser routes, downloadable databases and an OPTIMADE route. Provider states CMR databases use CC BY-SA 4.0. Portal totals are not an additional crystal dataset.

sources.title: CMR official portal
sources.evidence: Defines each project as an ASE database with a project page and browse/download access; links an OPTIMADE endpoint and states all CMR databases are CC BY-SA 4.0.

sources.title: 2DHub official portal
sources.evidence: Current home for C2DB and related 2D databases, links back to CMR; these named datasets are already separate catalog records.

name: Organic Materials Database (OMDB)
description: Electronic and magnetic information portal for periodic organic and organometallic crystals, including band structures, DOS and magnetic-excitation tools. Named downloads distinguish DFT-labelled OMDB-GAP1 from COD model predictions. Public browsing is limited and named downloads currently redirect to free-registration login; a current full-family count and dataset-wide reuse license were not verified.

sources.title: OMDB provider description
sources.evidence: Describes an organic/organometallic electronic-structure database with DFT and advanced query tools.

sources.title: OMDB named data releases
sources.evidence: Lists the 12,500-material OMDB-GAP1 and 260,092-material COD prediction releases as distinct products.

sources.title: OMDB terms
sources.evidence: Terms mention access quotas but do not identify a general data reuse license.

sources.title: OMDB public materials browser
sources.evidence: Anonymous browser explicitly limits visible data and offers free registration; the page-local displayed totals are not adopted as a full-family count.

name: MaterialsWeb
description: Hennig-group portal historically covering calculated 2D materials, bulk materials and computational benchmarks. Author paper released an 826-monolayer cohort in 2017. Current host failed TLS access in the 2026-11-01 audit, so live browsing, bulk downloads, current totals and data reuse rights remain unverified.

sources.title: Hennig Materials Theory Lab resources
sources.evidence: Provider lab explicitly links MaterialsWeb routes for 2D and bulk materials.

sources.title: Topology-Scaling Identification of Layered Solids and Stable Exfoliated 2D Materials
sources.evidence: Author paper identifies 826 monolayers and says optimized structures and related data were provided at MaterialsWeb; this is a historical paper cohort.

sources.title: MaterialsWeb direct access check
sources.evidence: Requested HTTPS host could not be fetched by the web tool; independent standard urllib access reported a TLS unrecognized-name failure for www and bare host.

name: NIST MGI Materials Data Resources
description: NIST directory of materials repositories, registries, schemas, phase-data resources and atomistic-potential services. It is a discovery resource, not an additional crystal dataset; access and reuse terms belong to each linked provider. Its Materials Resource Registry link currently redirects to the MGI landing page.

sources.title: NIST — Materials Data Resources
sources.evidence: Lists general repositories and registries, schemas, phase-based resources and an interatomic-potential repository, with separate descriptions and destinations.

sources.title: NIST Materials Resource Registry route
sources.evidence: The published registry endpoint resolved to https://www.nist.gov/mgi during this audit; this redirect does not establish formal end of service.

name: OpenKIM
description: Versioned archive of physics-based and machine-learning interatomic potentials, with model verification, property tests, simulation interfaces and a public query API. Crystal Genome organizes model-generated crystal-property predictions. Models and their test results must not be counted as independent experimentally measured or DFT-labeled crystals; an archive-wide data license was not verified.

sources.title: OpenKIM — About
sources.evidence: Describes the curated interatomic-potential archive, versioning and DOIs, KIM API, verification checks, and Crystal Genome property predictions using archived potentials.

sources.title: OpenKIM Query API
sources.evidence: Documents public queries over model, test and associated result records; these are different record types rather than a unique-crystal census.

sources.title: OpenKIM — Obtaining Models
sources.evidence: Provides public instructions for obtaining archived models, including package and source distribution routes.

name: PoLyInfo
description: NIMS literature-derived polymer properties with chemical constitutive structures, sample, preparation and measurement information. Chemical polymer structures do not imply periodic atomic crystal structures. Access requires DICE registration, an eligible email domain and a MatNavi usage application; bulk acquisition and scraping are prohibited, and redistribution requires written NIMS permission. A separate paid-dataset route is advertised.

sources.title: NIMS — PoLyInfo
sources.evidence: Describes polymer property and sample information; states account/application conditions, restrictions on mass acquisition and scraping, permission requirements for redistribution, and a fee-based dataset service.

name: Polymer Property Predictor and Database (PPPDB)
kind: adjacent polymer phase-property database and tools
description: CHiMaD-associated polymer data and prediction tools covering Flory–Huggins interaction parameters, glass-transition temperatures and cloud points, with phase-diagram and structure-factor applications. Public property tables were accessible without signing in. Periodic atomic structures and a database-wide reuse license were not verified.

sources.title: PPPDB — Polymer Property Predictor and Database
sources.evidence: Links polymer property databases and phase-diagram, random-phase structure-factor and cloud-point prediction applications; the HTTP endpoint upgrades to HTTPS.

sources.title: PPPDB — Flory–Huggins Interaction Parameter Database
sources.evidence: The public table presents polymer-pair interaction parameters, temperatures and literature references.

sources.title: PPPDB — Glass Transition Temperature Database
sources.evidence: A public table of polymer glass-transition data was accessible during the audit.

sources.title: PPPDB — Cloud Point Database
sources.evidence: A public cloud-point data table was accessible during the audit.

name: WebFF
kind: adjacent force-field repository and curation infrastructure
description: Documented repository for molecular-dynamics force-field parameters for organic and soft materials, using XML schemas and NIST curation infrastructure. Documentation describes public search/download and authorized-account curation. The documentation was reachable, but the live webff.nist.gov data portal could not be confirmed in this audit. Force-field parameterizations are not crystal datasets; a blanket data license was not verified.

sources.title: WebFF Documentation — Introduction
sources.evidence: Describes the force-field repository, organic/soft-material scope, XML provenance, exploration/download route and account-controlled curation route.

name: Configurable Data Curation System (CDCS / MDCS)
description: NIST software infrastructure for schema-based capture, sharing, transformation and federated discovery of structured scientific data. Materials Data Curation System is a materials-oriented implementation. It is not a standalone dataset: deployment-specific access and data terms apply. The software carries the NIST Software Licensing Statement, with separate third-party terms.

sources.title: NIST — About CDCS
sources.evidence: Describes XML-schema-driven data capture, curation and transformation, document storage and federation across curation instances; the user-supplied older organizational path resolves here.

sources.title: NIST — Materials Data Curation System source repository
sources.evidence: Provides the materials implementation and describes schema-generated forms, REST retrieval, document storage and federated search.

sources.title: MDCS — NIST Software Licensing Statement
sources.evidence: Permits use, modification and distribution subject to retaining the notice, marking changes and acknowledging NIST; third-party components have separate terms.

name: Polymer Properties Database (PolymerDatabase.com)
description: User-nominated polymer reference endpoint retained for discovery provenance. The requested page and HTTP, root-domain and www variants returned a hosting-provider page saying the site is temporarily unavailable, rather than polymer data, on the audit date. Original content, registration conditions and data licensing could not be verified; this observation is not a formal end-of-service claim.

sources.title: PolymerDatabase.com — current endpoint availability
sources.evidence: HTTP 200 response contained an iPage hosting-provider temporary-unavailability page; HTTP and HTTPS/root/www variants returned the same response body.

name: UCSD Superconducting Research Database (Schuller group)
description: Community database of materials tested for superconductivity, inviting researchers to upload results to reduce redundant testing. Live endpoint returned server errors during verification; current material/test counts, positive/negative/untested status definitions, crystal-file availability, uploader authentication and license remain unverified. This UCSD project is separate from NIST SRD 62.

sources.title: Schuller group: Foundation of New Superconducting Research Database
sources.evidence: Project-owning UCSD group identifies the SRD as a database of materials tested for superconductivity and invites researcher uploads to avoid redundant experiments.

sources.title: Schuller Nanoscience Group news archive
sources.evidence: Group news dates the database-foundation announcement to 13 March 2019.

sources.title: UCSD Superconducting Research Database
sources.evidence: Search-indexed primary interface exposes Name, Structure and Transition filters; direct requests returned HTTP 500 or timed out on the verification date. No current count or public bulk payload was verified.

name: Tran et al. review: Superconductor Discovery in the Emerging Paradigm of Materials Informatics
description: 2024 Chemistry of Materials review by Huan Tran, Hieu-Chi Dam, Christopher Kuenneth, Vu Ngoc Tuoc and Hiori Kino, 36(22), 10939–10966. Surveys computational hydrides and superconductivity informatics, including composition tables, structure matching, EPC computation and literature extraction. Used for discovery leads; current releases were checked at author repositories.

sources.title: ACS published review
sources.evidence: Publisher-indexed page verifies title, five authors, pages, online publication 8 November 2024 and CC BY 4.0. Direct publisher requests returned 403.

sources.title: Crossref publisher-deposited review metadata
sources.evidence: Confirms DOI, title, authors, 2024-11-08 publication and CC BY 4.0 version-of-record license.

sources.title: Author-posted full review manuscript
sources.evidence: Full manuscript is accessible; arXiv posting dated 29 October 2025 identifies the 2024 journal article. Dataset table identifies CompSC and the Stanev subset as leads.

sources.title: Author review figure data
sources.evidence: Author README identifies three CSV files for Figures 1, 3 and 15; these are figure-supporting files rather than a newly independent superconductor corpus.

name: NIST 62 / NIST–NRIM superconductors Version 2.0 publication
description: R. G. Munro’s NIST publication page (16 October 2008) documents evaluated superconducting, thermal, mechanical and crystallographic properties from 1987–1996 literature. Treated as documentation of the already cataloged NIST SRD 62 / WebHTS database family; the page does not establish a separate downloadable corpus or new release denominator.

sources.title: NIST 62. NIST/NRIM High Temperature Superconductors Database: Version 2.0
sources.evidence: Primary NIST publication metadata identifies R. G. Munro, 2008-10-16, evaluated properties and 1987–1996 source literature; it supplies no entry count or distinct downloadable dataset.

sources.title: NIST High Temperature Superconducting Materials Database search portal
sources.evidence: Same portal explicitly calls itself WebHTS and NIST Standard Reference Database 62, cites DOI 10.18434/T4KP8J and states last data-content update 1996.

sources.title: NIST WebHTS Version 2.0 publication (1999)
sources.evidence: Begley and Munro’s 1999 page describes the same evaluated oxide-superconductor property families; separate publication dates do not establish independent dataset releases.
